views.name: dim_customer_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code,
  customer,
  platform,
  channel,
  market,
  sub_zone,
  region
FROM hardware_dim_customer

params.when_to_use: Lookup stable customer attributes by customer_code (e.g., attach customer name, platform, channel, market, sub_zone, region to a row-level dataset keyed by customer_code). | Build dimension joins in star-schema queries where each row of the fact is one customer_code and you need descriptive fields (customer, platform, channel, market, sub_zone, region) without changing cardinality. | Filter or group at the customer_code grain (e.g., count distinct customers, list customers in a market or region).
params.when_not_to_use: When you need measurements at a different grain (e.g., customer × date, customer × product, or aggregated metrics): reusing this view and then aggregating may silently drop/detail-mismatch rows because this view has one row per customer_code only. | When you need cohorted or time-bounded customer membership (e.g., customers active during a month or first-purchase cohort): this view has no temporal columns and does not represent membership over time, so joining it to time-based facts can overstate or understate cohorts. | When you need account/rep-level or organizational role information: this view exposes only customer descriptive columns and not account/rep relationships (use dim_accounts_with_reps or a joinable account view instead). | When you need sales or transactional measures (revenue, quantity, prices): this is a pure dimension (no measures). Reusing it in place of a fact or enriched fact will produce incorrect numeric results. | When you need de-duplicated customers by any alternate key (e.g., customer name or platform-specific id): the declared grain is customer_code; if the source hardware_dim_customer contains duplicates or changing keys, reusing without verifying uniqueness will cause mis-counting.
params.comparison: use dim_product_base instead when you need product dimension attributes rather than customer attributes — it has the same NORM role (dimension) but provides product-level columns rather than customer-level ones. | use dim_accounts_with_reps instead when you need account or sales-rep relationships for customers — it is a JOIN view that includes account/rep context which dim_customer_base does not provide. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched or fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal when you need monthly sales measures or aggregated sales metrics — those are AGG/JOIN facts and contain measures and time grain which this customer dimension does not. | use web_orders_ranked or orders_timeseries_measures when you need order-level ordering, ranking, or time-series measures — those AGG/RANK views include transactional/time detail that dim_customer_base lacks.

views.description: Cleaned/passed-through customer dimension. Use when joining sales or deduction facts to customer descriptive attributes (market, region, platform, channel). Preserves original customer_code key and canonicalizes NULLs. | Use for: Aggregate sales by market/region/platform; Filter customers by channel or platform; Join customer attributes to monthly sales, deductions, or prices

views.name: dim_product_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code,
  division,
  segment,
  category,
  product,
  variant
FROM hardware_dim_product

params.when_to_use: Lookup the canonical attributes of a product when you need one row per product_code (e.g., show product name, division, segment, category, product variant for a given product_code). | Join onto product-level dimensions to enrich fact records that are at the product_code grain (e.g., attach product attributes to fact_sales_monthly_enriched rows that already have product_code). | Build reports or UI lists that display product metadata (catalog pages, filters, dropdowns) where duplicates per product_code would be incorrect. | Validate or de-duplicate product keys when you need the authoritative set of product_code values and their current attributes.
params.when_not_to_use: When you need product pricing, cost, or temporal attributes (e.g., price or cost by year) — this view contains no price/cost or time-varying columns; using it will miss those dimensions and silently drop needed information. | When you need an aggregated measure across products (sales totals, counts) — this is a dimension at product_code grain, not an aggregation; joining it into aggregations without grouping by product_code can cause row-multiplying or incorrect sums. | When you need product history or time-variant attributes (effective dates, price history, variant changes) — this view has only current/static attributes; reusing it assumes attributes are stable and can silently produce incorrect temporal joins. | When you need product rows scoped to a cohort or filter stored elsewhere (e.g., only products sold in a period) — this view returns all rows from hardware_dim_product; using it as if it were already filtered will include out-of-cohort products. | When you need a non-unique grain (e.g., multiple rows per product for different SKUs or sizes) — this view's declared grain is product_code; if hardware_dim_product actually contains duplicates for a product_code, relying on uniqueness will miscount rows.
params.comparison: use product_price_cost_yearly instead when you need price or cost broken down by year — dim_product_base has the static product attributes but product_price_cost_yearly contains the temporal pricing/cost measures. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched or fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need sales measures by time period — those sibling views contain aggregated sales measures and time grain; dim_product_base is only a product attribute table and has no measures or time dimensions. | use web_orders_ranked or orders_timeseries_measures when you need order-level or time-series aggregations tied to products — those siblings include ordering/time measures and pre-aggregated metrics, whereas dim_product_base only supplies descriptive product fields to join on. | use dim_customer_base or dim_accounts_with_reps when your join target is customer/account-level data — those siblings are customer/account dimensions with appropriate grains; dim_product_base is for product-level enrichment and is not a substitute for customer/account dimensions.

views.description: Product dimension pass-through. Use when analyzing product-level measures (price, cost, sales) by division/segment/category/variant. | Use for: Roll up sales/cost/price by product category or segment; Filter products by variant or division; Enrich monthly sales with product attributes

views.name: fact_sales_monthly_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.date,
  s.product_code,
  s.customer_code,
  s.sold_quantity,
  s.fiscal_year,
  c.customer AS customer,
  c.platform AS platform,
  c.channel AS channel,
  c.market AS market,
  c.sub_zone AS sub_zone,
  c.region AS region,
  p.division AS division,
  p.segment AS segment,
  p.category AS category,
  p.product AS product,
  p.variant AS variant
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly s
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_customer c
  ON s.customer_code = c.customer_code
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_product p
  ON s.product_code = p.product_code

params.when_to_use: Calculate metrics (sums, averages, counts) at the monthly product × customer × date grain — e.g., "how many units of product X did customer Y purchase in 2023-04" or "monthly sold_quantity per product_code and customer_code". | Join this monthly sales detail to other tables expecting one row per (date, product_code, customer_code) — e.g., to attribute a monthly sale to a customer or product dimension without inflating counts. | Filter by customer or product attributes that exist on the joined dimension rows (platform, channel, market, division, category, etc.) when you need those attributes alongside the monthly sale record. | Compute time-series trends or rollups that start from the monthly sales detail before aggregating up (but only if you re-aggregate explicitly to the desired higher grain).
params.when_not_to_use: As a source for customer- or product-level aggregates without re-aggregation — WHY: the view is at the (date, product_code, customer_code) grain. Summing across rows without grouping will double-count if you assume a different grain (for example, treating it as one row per product or one row per customer). | As a cohort table to represent all customers or products — WHY: it is a LEFT JOIN of sales to dimensions, so customers/products without sales in a month are absent. It does not represent the full customer/product base (use the dimension base views instead). | For analyses that require canonical dimension attributes guaranteed to exist (inner-join semantics) — WHY: joins are LEFT JOINs from fact to dims; dimension columns will be NULL for codes in the fact that have no matching dim row, so filtering/logic expecting non-null dimension values may silently drop or misclassify rows. | When selecting distinct customers or products for a master list (membership/cohort) — WHY: view only contains customers/products that had sales in the monthly fact; using it as the master list will omit zero-sales entities. | As a deduplicated transactions table where unique sale identifiers are expected — WHY: the underlying schema exposes no transaction_id and the grain is monthly aggregated sold_quantity; you cannot use this to count individual invoices or events. | When you need fiscal- or calendar-level aggregation already rolled up by fiscal year or other aggregation windows — WHY: this view exposes fiscal_year per monthly row but is not pre-aggregated to fiscal totals (use an AGG sibling if available). | For row-level joins that assume every product_code/customer_code combination is unique per date in the source — WHY: the view is built from hardware_fact_sales_monthly; if that source contains multiple rows per (date,product_code,customer_code) then this view will reflect that multiplicity (it does not deduplicate).
params.comparison: use dim_customer_base instead when you need a complete, canonical customer roster — it is a normalized dimension (NORM) and includes customers regardless of whether they appear in sales; fact_sales_monthly_enriched only contains customers with sales in the fact. | use dim_product_base instead when you need a complete, canonical product roster or authoritative product attributes — it is a normalized product dimension (NORM); the enriched view only has product rows present in the monthly sales fact and may have NULL attributes when the LEFT JOIN fails. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need pre-aggregated fiscal-year sales metrics — that sibling is an AGG at fiscal aggregation (saves re-aggregation and avoids errors from aggregating monthly rows incorrectly). | use product_price_cost_yearly instead when your analysis requires yearly price/cost attributes joined at year granularity — the enriched view joins product attributes at the monthly sales grain and is not aligned to yearly price/cost records. | use pre_invoice_deductions_by_customer_year when you need customer-level yearly adjustments or deductions — that sibling is normalized/aggregated for customer-year adjustments, whereas this view is monthly sales detail and will not reflect separate deduction aggregates. | use orders_timeseries_measures or web_events_daily_counts when you require event/order-level or daily aggregations — those AGG views are already aggregated at different time grains (daily/other) and avoid errors from mis-aligning monthly data to different time windows.

views.description: Monthly sales fact joined to customer and product dimensions and fiscal year exposed. Useful as the starting wide relation for revenue/quantity analyses by customer/product attributes. | Use for: Compute total sold_quantity by market/region/category; Filter monthly sales for customers or products with particular attributes; Join to price/cost facts to compute margin per product/customer

views.name: fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code,
  customer_code,
  fiscal_year,
  SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_sold_quantity,
  COUNT(*) AS months_reported
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly
GROUP BY product_code, customer_code, fiscal_year

params.when_to_use: When you need total quantity sold and how many monthly rows contributed, aggregated at the level of product_code × customer_code × fiscal_year (e.g., “How many units of product X did customer Y buy in fiscal year Z, and in how many monthly records were those sales recorded?”). | When the business question is explicitly about fiscal-year totals per product and customer (reporting, invoicing summaries, annual customer-product performance). | When downstream logic will re-aggregate these pre-aggregated rows only across full (product_code, customer_code, fiscal_year) keys (e.g., summing total_sold_quantity across multiple views that partition by fiscal_year).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view when you need a different grain (e.g., monthly, daily, per-order, per-invoice, or per-customer-year without product): this view has been aggregated to product_code × customer_code × fiscal_year and will silently undercount rows and over-aggregate counts if used where finer granularity is required. | Do not use as a source for calculations that assume months_reported is the number of distinct months in the fiscal year unless you have verified the base table has exactly one row per product/customer/month: months_reported is COUNT(*) of grouped source rows, not COUNT(DISTINCT month). If the source can have multiple rows per month this will overstate months reported. | Do not use to compute customer- or product-level totals that should ignore the other dimension (e.g., total per product across all customers) unless you explicitly re-aggregate and understand that months_reported will not meaningfully aggregate across collapsed dimensions (COUNT(*) aggregates will sum the counts of underlying groups, which is not equivalent to counting distinct months across the larger set). | Do not use when you need time-series at monthly resolution: the view removes the month dimension and so cannot be used for month-by-month trends without losing information. | Do not use when you need non-fiscal-year calendars (calendar year, rolling 12 months) — the fiscal_year field is the grouping key and any shift in period definition will be incorrect.
params.comparison: use fact_sales_monthly_enriched instead when you need row-level (monthly) detail or enriched attributes from joins — it preserves monthly rows and joins to dimension data so you can compute distinct-month counts and more precise cohorts. | use orders_timeseries_measures instead when you need correctly-handled timeseries aggregations over time (e.g., month-by-month measures or rolling windows) — that view is designed for time-series aggregations rather than fiscal-year collapsed aggregates. | use product_price_cost_yearly instead when you are answering questions that combine sales totals with yearly price/cost metrics — it aligns product-year measures (price/cost) to a yearly grain and avoids mixing fiscal-year sales that might use a different year boundary. | use dim_customer_base or dim_product_base when you need canonical customer or product attributes, or to filter cohorts before aggregating — this AGG view does not include dimension attributes and may produce wrong cohorts if filtering happens after aggregation. | use web_orders_ranked or web_events_daily_counts when your analysis depends on ranking or day-level counts — those siblings handle ordering/ranking and daily aggregation respectively, which this fiscal-year aggregate does not support.

views.description: Aggregated monthly sales measures rolled up to product_code x customer_code x fiscal_year. Provides total sold quantity per fiscal year and preserved keys for joining to yearly pricing/cost/deductions. | Use for: Annual sales volume per product or customer; Join annual sales to annual price/cost/deduction tables; Compute year-over-year changes in sold quantity

views.name: dim_accounts_with_reps
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id,
  a.name,
  a.website,
  a.lat,
  a.long,
  a.primary_poc,
  a.sales_rep_id,
  r.name AS region_name,
  s.name AS sales_rep_name
FROM web_accounts a
LEFT JOIN web_sales_reps s
  ON a.sales_rep_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN web_region r
  ON s.region_id = r.id

params.when_to_use: Get one row per account (account-level grain) including basic account attributes and its assigned sales rep and region — e.g., 'list accounts with their primary sales rep and region'. | Join account attributes into other account-grain facts or dimension-enriched fact tables when you need the stable account id, name, website, coordinates, primary point-of-contact, sales_rep_id and the rep/region display names. | Report/lookup use cases where no aggregation is required and you want NULL-safe rep/region when an account has no assigned rep (LEFT JOIN semantics preserve the account row).
params.when_not_to_use: When you need aggregates (counts, sums, averages) across transactions or time — this view is at the account grain, so aggregating without re-checking joins may double-count if joined to many-to-one fact tables; use an aggregated fact view instead. | When you need account cohorts filtered by events/orders/time windows — this view does not restrict cohort membership or include event/order rows; reusing it as if it represented 'accounts with orders in period X' will silently include accounts with no orders because it has no order filter. | When you need a different grain (customer–product, account–month, order-level, or sales-rep-level) — reusing it in place of a view at a finer or coarser grain will produce incorrect counts or averages (e.g., JOINing this directly to orders and then aggregating without deduping account attributes may inflate results). | When you need authoritative sales rep metadata beyond name/id/region id (e.g., rep territory definitions, rep manager, active/inactive status) — this view only selects s.name and s.id and relies on web_sales_reps LEFT JOIN; missing columns or business rules live elsewhere. | When you require enforced referential integrity to only include accounts that have sales reps — this view uses LEFT JOIN to preserve accounts without reps; using it when you need inner-join semantics will include extra rows (accounts without reps).
params.comparison: use dim_customer_base instead when you need a canonical customer normalization (NORM) or additional canonical customer keys and standardized attribute transformations — dim_accounts_with_reps is a JOIN that adds rep/region names but is not the canonical normalized customer record. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need aggregated monthly fiscal sales measures at account or fiscal period grain — dim_accounts_with_reps provides only account attributes and will not provide correct aggregated sales totals. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched when you need account attributes already pre-joined to monthly sales facts (JOIN) — that fact view is oriented to time-series measures and avoids the need to join this dimension to facts and risk of cardinality errors. | use web_orders_ranked when you need order-level or ranked-order results — dim_accounts_with_reps is account-level and will not preserve order-level detail or ranking within orders. | use product_price_cost_yearly or pre_invoice_deductions_by_customer_year when you require yearly product-level or invoice-deduction aggregates — those views are aggregated or product-scoped; reusing the account-level view would miss the aggregation logic and cohort filters. | use course_offering_enrollments or student_transcript_view when working with educational enrollments/transcripts — those sibling JOIN views are domain-specific and include enrollment-level grain; dim_accounts_with_reps is unrelated in grain and domain and will produce incorrect joins/filters if substituted.

views.description: Accounts enriched with sales rep and region names. Use when relating web orders or events to account-level sales representative and region data. | Use for: Order/event counts by sales rep or region; Map accounts by lat/long and sales rep; Filter accounts for CRM follow-up by sales rep

views.name: orders_timeseries_measures
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  date(substr(occurred_at,1,10)) AS occurred_date,
  account_id,
  SUM(standard_qty) AS sum_standard_qty,
  SUM(gloss_qty) AS sum_gloss_qty,
  SUM(poster_qty) AS sum_poster_qty,
  SUM(total) AS sum_total_qty,
  SUM(standard_amt_usd) AS sum_standard_amt_usd,
  SUM(gloss_amt_usd) AS sum_gloss_amt_usd,
  SUM(poster_amt_usd) AS sum_poster_amt_usd,
  SUM(total_amt_usd) AS sum_total_amt_usd,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_count
FROM web_orders
GROUP BY occurred_date, account_id

params.when_to_use: Time-series of order-level measures aggregated to the day and account: use when you need daily totals per account (e.g., daily quantity or USD amount sold to an account). | Counting number of web_orders rows per account per day: use when orders_count = number of rows is the desired metric (each web_orders row represents one order). | Summing the provided *_qty or *_amt_usd columns for trend, per-account reporting, or downstream aggregations that will respect the day+account grain (for example producing daily revenue or volume charts per account). | Feeding into dashboards or pipelines that require pre-aggregated daily-account level measures (reducing volume compared with raw web_orders).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need order-level detail (order id, timestamps, line-item detail, or per-order attributes) — this view aggregates away per-order identity so you cannot slice back to individual orders. | Do not use when you need a different time grain than date(occurred_at) (e.g., hour, week-start, month, or fiscal month) — the view collapses time to calendar date using date(substr(occurred_at,1,10)). Reusing it for hourly or monthly analysis will silently misrepresent timing. | Do not use when your cohort/filter is at a finer or different grain than account_id (for example customer_id, product_id, store_id, or sales_rep) — the view aggregates by account_id only. Filtering by those other keys after aggregation can produce incorrect cohorts or double-counting. | Do not use when you need distinct counts of orders by an order identifier (COUNT(*) here counts rows in web_orders; if web_orders can contain multiple rows per order or if you need COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) this will overcount). | Do not use when you intend to join this view to other tables expecting the raw web_orders row semantics (joins that assume one row per order may multiply aggregates because of aggregation before join). | Do not use when you need measures derived from columns not present in this view (e.g., taxes, discounts, or per-line metrics) — those fields are not available and cannot be reconstructed. | Do not use when comparing to other aggregated results that use a different definition of occurred_date (e.g., timezone-aware truncation or fiscal date functions) — date(substr(...)) may differ from other date-truncation methods.
params.comparison: use web_orders_ranked instead when you need order-level ranking, deduplication, or to select a canonical row per order — web_orders_ranked preserves row-level identity and ranking logic, whereas orders_timeseries_measures is already aggregated to day+account. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need consistent fiscal-month aggregation — fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal provides aggregation at a fiscal-month grain, while orders_timeseries_measures is calendar-date daily and will not match fiscal-month totals without re-aggregation and careful date mapping. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched when you need month-level enriched sales measures joined to dimensional attributes — fact_sales_monthly_enriched is designed for monthly summaries and enrichment, whereas orders_timeseries_measures provides raw daily-account sums without enrichment. | use dim_accounts_with_reps when your filtering or grouping needs account metadata (sales rep, territory) before aggregating — dim_accounts_with_reps contains account attributes to correctly define cohorts or joins; joining those attributes after using this aggregated view may hide or misapply filtering intended to happen at the raw-row level. | use web_events_daily_counts when you want event-based daily counts (same daily aggregation pattern) but for web events instead of orders — both are daily AGG views, but they operate on different source semantics (events vs orders).

views.description: Orders aggregated at date (day) level with revenue and quantity measures. Useful for time-series analysis, trends, and joining to account attributes. | Use for: Daily revenue/time-series per account; Trend analysis of quantity types (standard/gloss/poster); Join daily orders to account or region attributes

views.name: staff_event_intervals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  StaffMember,
  EventDate,
  EventTime AS event_time,
  EventType,
  -- combine date and time into an ISO-like timestamp for ordering
  datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime) AS event_ts,
  LAG(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) AS prev_event_type,
  LAG(datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) AS prev_event_ts,
  CASE
    WHEN EventType = 'Exit' AND LAG(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) = 'Enter'
    THEN (strftime('%s', datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) - strftime('%s', LAG(datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime))))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS interval_seconds
FROM StaffHours

params.when_to_use: Compute per-staff, per-calendar-date ordered event sequences (e.g., show each timestamped sign-in/sign-out event for a staff member for a single date). | Measure interval between an Exit event and the immediately preceding Enter event that occur on the same StaffMember and same EventDate (e.g., calculate time on-site per Enter→Exit pair within one day). | Produce event-level detail for downstream logic that needs previous-event type or previous-event timestamp within the same day (e.g., classify event transitions or detect back-to-back duplicate events). | Power visualizations or tables that list events at the StaffMember / EventDate / EventTime grain (no further aggregation).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view when you need durations that span midnight or multiple calendar dates — it partitions by EventDate, so prior events on the previous/next date are excluded, causing undercounted or missing intervals. | Avoid using it to compute total time per StaffMember across a day, week, or other period by naively summing interval_seconds without checking for NULLs and Enter/Exit pairing — interval_seconds is only populated for Exit rows whose immediate previous event on that same date is Enter; other patterns (Enter→Enter, Exit→Exit, missing Enter) yield NULL and will mis-count if not handled explicitly. | Do not reuse this view for analyses at any coarser grain (e.g., per-staff daily aggregates, weekly totals, headcount) without an explicit aggregation query that documents how to handle NULL intervals, overlapping events, and multi-day spans — using it as if it were already aggregated will produce silently-wrong results. | Do not use it to extract absolute event timestamps in a timezone-aware or reliably parsable canonical timestamp format beyond the SQLite-compatible datetime string produced here; the view builds timestamps with string concatenation of EventDate and EventTime which may mis-order or mis-parse if EventDate/EventTime formats differ from expectations. | Do not use it when you need full session reconstruction where an Enter may pair with the next Exit even if intervening events exist (this view only pairs Exit with the immediately preceding event and requires that previous event to be Enter). | Avoid reusing for cohort filters that are not strictly per-EventDate (for example, 'events in the last 24 hours') because partitioning and ordering are per EventDate and will not link events across date boundaries.
params.comparison: use dim_customer_base instead when you need normalized master/entity attributes for customers rather than event sequences — dim_customer_base is a normalization (NORM) view for entity attributes, while staff_event_intervals is event-level time-series. | use orders_timeseries_measures instead when you need time-series aggregated measures over periods (AGG) rather than row-level event durations — orders_timeseries_measures aggregates and is safe for period-level metrics while staff_event_intervals is raw event rows. | use web_events_daily_counts when you want daily aggregated event counts (AGG) rather than per-event detail — web_events_daily_counts provides pre-aggregated, day-level counts, preventing the risk of double-counting that would occur if you aggregated staff_event_intervals incorrectly. | use web_orders_ranked when you need ranked ordering across a broader partition/window — web_orders_ranked is a RANK-style view for ordering within a partition, while staff_event_intervals only uses LAG to access the immediately prior row within StaffMember and EventDate. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal or orders_timeseries_measures when your goal is monthly/fiscal aggregated measures (AGG) instead of event-level intervals — those sibling AGG views are pre-aggregated and handle period bucketing that this view does not.

views.description: Pairs Enter/Exit events into intervals per StaffMember and EventDate using LAG/LEAD. Exposes interval start/end and duration (seconds). Useful for computing worked hours or session durations. | Use for: Compute total worked seconds per staff per day; Identify unmatched Enter or Exit events; Analyze session length distributions

views.name: faculty_salary_roster
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  FacNo,
  FacFirstName,
  FacLastName,
  FacCity,
  FacState,
  FacDept,
  FacRank,
  FacSalary,
  FacSupervisor,
  date(FacHireDate) AS FacHireDate,
  FacZipCode
FROM university_faculty

params.when_to_use: Get one row per faculty member (FacNo) with basic demographic and employment attributes — e.g., show roster details for each faculty person. | Join faculty attributes to another table at the faculty-person grain (FacNo) without changing cardinality — e.g., enrich a fact table that already uses FacNo as the foreign key. | Display or export contact/hire information for faculty (name, city/state/zip, department, rank, supervisor, hire date, salary) for reporting or directory purposes. | Filter or slice faculty by attributes in this view (FacDept, FacRank, FacState, FacHireDate) when your intent is to select individual faculty members rather than to summarize them.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use this view when you need aggregated metrics (counts, sums, averages) across faculty groups — WHY: the view is at the individual-faculty grain and has one row per FacNo; aggregating without explicit GROUP BY or understanding will risk double-counting or under-counting. | Avoid using this view to represent headcounts/cohorts over time or time-series trends — WHY: it contains a single FacHireDate (cast to date) and no history or temporal granularity; it is not a timeseries or interval table and will be silently wrong for longitudinal analyses. | Do not reuse for enrollment/teaching or course-related metrics — WHY: it contains no course, section, term, or enrollment columns; joining it to course-level data without careful join keys can change cardinality and produce inflated results. | Do not use when you need payroll or compensation history across periods (e.g., salary by month/year) — WHY: FacSalary appears as a current/static value from university_faculty, no effective-dating or versioning is provided; reusing it for periodized salary aggregates will produce incorrect time allocations. | Avoid using as a filter source for non-faculty entities (customers, products, orders) — WHY: the view's cohort is faculty only; applying it as if it represented customers, accounts, or web users will mismap keys and cohorts and produce empty or misleading joins. | Do not assume uniqueness beyond FacNo as provided — WHY: the statement selects from university_faculty but does not declare constraints; if source contains duplicate FacNo, downstream joins/aggregations could unexpectedly duplicate rows.
params.comparison: use dim_accounts_with_reps instead when you need account ownership/rep information for customers/accounts — it is a JOINed view that has account-level relationships; faculty_salary_roster is person/faculty-level and lacks account keys. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need monthly or fiscal-period aggregated measures (sales totals) — that view is AGG and time-bucketed; faculty_salary_roster is a non-aggregated roster and not suitable for period aggregations. | use staff_event_intervals instead when you need interval/timespan information about staff events (tenure periods, leaves) — staff_event_intervals is a WIN/interval-oriented view; faculty_salary_roster only provides a single hire date and no interval semantics. | use student_transcript_view when combining faculty info with student course performance or transcript-level analytics — student_transcript_view is JOINed to course/student records; faculty_salary_roster has no course or student linkage and will not preserve the correct join grain for transcript analyses. | use product_price_cost_yearly or fact_sales_monthly_enriched when combining with product or sales facts — those sibling views are designed for product or sales contexts (JOIN/AGG); faculty_salary_roster is unrelated in domain and lacks product/order keys.

views.description: Faculty roster with hire date parsed and salary exposed. Use when analyzing salary distributions by department, rank, or hire date. | Use for: Average salary by FacDept or FacRank; Hire-date based tenure or service calculations; Supervisor hierarchy joins

views.name: course_offering_enrollments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.OfferNo,
  e.StdNo,
  e.EnrGrade,
  o.CourseNo,
  o.OffTerm,
  o.OffYear,
  o.OffLocation,
  o.OffTime,
  o.FacNo,
  o.OffDays,
  c.CrsDesc,
  c.CrsUnits
FROM university_enrollment e
LEFT JOIN university_offering o
  ON e.OfferNo = o.OfferNo
LEFT JOIN university_course c
  ON o.CourseNo = c.CourseNo

params.when_to_use: Get one row per student enrollment in a specific offering (OfferNo, StdNo) including the student's grade and the offering/course attributes — e.g., list all students enrolled in offering 123 with their EnrGrade and the course/offering metadata. | Join to other row-level enrollment facts keyed by OfferNo+StdNo (for example to add attendance or fee rows) when you need a true enrollment-level fact table. | Build detailed enrollment exports, reconciliation or CSV extracts where each enrollment must appear even if course metadata is missing (LEFT JOIN preserves enrollments).
params.when_not_to_use: As a course-level roster or to count enrollments per offering — the view is grain OfferNo+StdNo, so aggregating counts without DISTINCT or GROUP BY StdNo will risk double-counting if you join other tables later; use an explicit aggregation on StdNo to get unique student counts. | To answer questions about offerings that require only offering-level attributes (one row per OfferNo) — using this view will return multiple rows per offering (one per student) and can silently inflate results when aggregated without grouping by OfferNo. | As a student-centric history (one row per StdNo) — the view repeats a student across multiple offerings; reuse will be wrong for student-level metrics unless you further aggregate or filter to a single OfferNo. | To filter reliably on course attributes when relying on the presence of course data — the view uses LEFT JOIN from enrollment to offering and then to course, so missing offering or course rows will produce NULL course fields; queries that expect INNER-JOIN semantics may silently include enrollments with NULL CourseNo/CrsDesc. | When you need guaranteed completeness of offering metadata (e.g., to ensure OffTime/FacNo always exist) — because the join starts from enrollments, offerings without enrollments are not present at all, and offering-only questions will miss those offerings.
params.comparison: use student_transcript_view instead when you need enrollment history aggregated or normalized by student (it is a JOIN sibling focused on transcript-level semantics) — this view is enrollment-row-grained while student_transcript_view likely presents transcript-oriented columns and may handle course repeats/term logic. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal (AGG) as an example pattern when you need pre-aggregated counts per offering (replace sales by enrollments) — course_offering_enrollments is a JOIN at the enrollment grain, whereas an AGG sibling would return one row per offering with aggregated measures. | use dim_product_base or dim_customer_base (NORM) when you need stable dimensional records (one row per CourseNo or per StdNo) — those NORM siblings provide a normalized, single-row-per-entity shape; course_offering_enrollments repeats CourseNo and StdNo across rows. | use orders_timeseries_measures (AGG) when you want time-series measures already rolled up by term/year — course_offering_enrollments contains OffTerm/OffYear per enrollment but is not pre-aggregated into time-series metrics and will require grouping to produce comparable results.

views.description: Enrollment bridge joined to offering and course metadata. One row per enrollment (OfferNo x StdNo) with course and offering attributes exposed for term/year analyses. | Use for: Grade distributions by course/term/year; Student transcripts or performance over offerings; Instructor load by offering/year

views.name: product_price_cost_yearly
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_code,
  gp.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  gp.gross_price AS gross_price,
  mc.manufacturing_cost AS manufacturing_cost
FROM hardware_fact_gross_price gp
LEFT JOIN hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost mc
  ON gp.product_code = mc.product_code
  AND gp.fiscal_year = mc.cost_year
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_product p
  ON gp.product_code = p.product_code

params.when_to_use: Calculate or report annual gross price and manufacturing cost for each product_code in the hardware product catalog — e.g., "show gross_price and manufacturing_cost for product X in fiscal year Y." | Join to other product-level yearly analyses where the desired grain is exactly product_code + fiscal_year (no additional time or customer dimensions). | Detect changes in per-product yearly listed gross_price vs manufacturing_cost (row-level comparison at product_code × fiscal_year).
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need a different grain such as monthly, daily, per-order, per-customer, or per-sale. This view is aggregated at product_code × fiscal_year; reusing it for sub-year (monthly/daily) analyses will hide intra-year variation and produce silently incorrect results. | Do not use when you need totals or averages across multiple products or years without explicit aggregation. The view returns one row per product_code × fiscal_year; summing or averaging those rows without considering missing products or duplicate keys in source tables can mis-count or double-count values. | Do not use when you need manufacturing_cost or gross_price defined for a different year alignment (e.g., cost_year vs fiscal_year mismatch). The manufacturing_cost is joined where mc.cost_year = gp.fiscal_year; if your question expects a different cost-year alignment (lagged costs, calendar year, or cost effective date), reuse will be wrong. | Do not use when you need the inner join semantics for cost or product existence. The view LEFT JOINs manufacturing_cost and product dimension to gross_price, preserving rows from hardware_fact_gross_price. If you require only products that have manufacturing_cost or only known product dimension rows, this view will include extra NULLs and lead to incorrect cohorts unless you filter them explicitly. | Do not use when you need row-level measures tied to sales/orders/customers. This view has no customer, order, or sales identifiers — reusing it to represent transactional measures (e.g., revenue or per-order cost) will be silently incorrect. | Do not use when you expect non-NULL guarantees. Because manufacturing_cost and product fields come from LEFT JOINs, NULLs indicate missing matches; assuming non-NULL values will produce incorrect calculations.
params.comparison: use dim_product_base instead when you need canonical product attributes or to filter/lookup product metadata — dim_product_base is a normalized product dimension; product_price_cost_yearly includes prices and costs joined from facts and is not authoritative for static product attributes. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need monthly or aggregated sales measures by fiscal year — that view provides time-bucketed sales aggregates; product_price_cost_yearly is at product×fiscal_year for price/cost only and lacks sales aggregation. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched instead when you need transactional or monthly sales context joined to prices/costs — fact_sales_monthly_enriched contains richer sales context and a different grain (monthly sales) suitable for revenue or per-order metrics. | use orders_timeseries_measures when you require time-series aggregates over orders (e.g., revenue over time) — orders_timeseries_measures is an aggregation over orders and time, while product_price_cost_yearly is not an orders measure and would misrepresent order-based metrics. | use dim_customer_base or pre_invoice_deductions_by_customer_year when your cohort is defined by customers or customer-year totals — product_price_cost_yearly is product-year and has no customer dimensions, so it cannot represent customer cohorts.

views.description: Yearly product-level price and manufacturing cost joined together. Use when computing per-unit margin by product and year after joining to sales aggregates. | Use for: Compute per-unit margin = gross_price - manufacturing_cost; Price and cost trend analysis by product and fiscal_year; Join to annual sales to compute gross margin dollars

views.name: pre_invoice_deductions_by_customer_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code,
  fiscal_year,
  pre_invoice_discount_pct
FROM hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions

params.when_to_use: Calculate or report the pre-invoice discount percentage per customer per fiscal year (e.g., "what was each customer's pre-invoice discount pct in fiscal year 2024?"). | Join this view when you need a single row per customer per fiscal year to annotate other annual customer-level measures (e.g., merge with yearly revenue to compute effective discounted revenue per customer-year). | Produce tables, exports, or dashboards that display the discount percent at the customer-by-fiscal-year grain without further aggregation.
params.when_not_to_use: When you need discounts at a lower time grain (month/day) — this view has fiscal_year as its time grain and will silently drop intra-year variance if reused for monthly analyses. | When you need per-invoice or per-order discount percentages — this view is aggregated to customer × fiscal_year and cannot represent invoice-level variation; reusing it will mis-count or hide variability across invoices. | When you need a cohort filtered by attributes not present here (for example product, account rep, or sales territory) — those dimensions are not available, so filtering/joining after reuse can produce incorrect cohorts or cause accidental row-multiplication. | When you plan to aggregate the view again without careful aggregation logic (for example summing pre_invoice_discount_pct across customers or years) — pre_invoice_discount_pct is a percentage already summarized at customer-year and naïve aggregation will produce meaningless results. | When you expect multiple rows per customer-year (for example different discounts by product or account) — this view exposes exactly one row per customer_code × fiscal_year from hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions; if the source actually contains multiple rows they have already been resolved, and reusing the view to reconstruct detail is impossible.
params.comparison: use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need time-partitioned sales or discounts by month within a fiscal year — it has a finer time grain (monthly) while pre_invoice_deductions_by_customer_year is annual. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched when you need invoice/order-level or monthly sales context joined to discounts — fact_sales_monthly_enriched is a JOIN that contains richer transactional/contextual fields; pre_invoice_deductions_by_customer_year only provides the customer-year percentage. | use dim_customer_base when you need customer attributes (name, segment, territory) to form cohorts or filters — dim_customer_base is a normalized dimension with customer attributes, whereas this view only supplies customer_code and the aggregated discount pct. | use product_price_cost_yearly when your analysis must attribute discounts to product-level pricing or cost in the same fiscal year — product_price_cost_yearly provides product-year pricing context that this customer-year discount view lacks.

views.description: Per-customer per-year pre-invoice discount percentages. Use to apply discount rates to annual sales when computing net revenue. | Use for: Apply pre-invoice discounts to annual sales by customer; Analyze discount rates by customer or market

views.name: web_events_daily_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  date(substr(occurred_at,1,10)) AS occurred_date,
  account_id,
  channel,
  COUNT(*) AS events_count
FROM web_events
GROUP BY occurred_date, account_id, channel

params.when_to_use: Counting raw web events per account per channel for each calendar date — e.g., “How many web events did account 123 generate on 2024-05-01 on the email channel?” | Time-series or trend charts at the daily granularity partitioned by account and channel — e.g., daily event counts per account and channel for plotting or downstream aggregation to weekly/monthly after explicit aggregation. | Joins where you need the daily count as an input metric keyed by (occurred_date, account_id, channel) — e.g., joining to an account lookup to report daily events per account-channel.
params.when_not_to_use: When you need event counts at a different grain (user/session/order/product) — the view is aggregated to occurred_date × account_id × channel. Using it for per-user or per-session metrics will under- or over-count because those finer-grain identities are lost. | When you need counts scoped by arbitrary filters on occurred_at timestamps (time-of-day, timezone-aware day boundaries, or non-calendar-day windows) — the view derives occurred_date by casting the first 10 chars of occurred_at to date; that implicit truncation may not match your desired boundary and removes the original timestamp. | When you need deduplicated events (unique users, unique sessions, distinct event types) — the view uses COUNT(*) on raw rows, so any deduplication or distinct counting must be done from the base table, not from this aggregated view. | When you expect fiscal or month-level aggregations already adjusted for business calendars — this view is strictly calendar-date daily counts; aggregating to months or fiscal periods from it is possible but requires care about how date→period mapping is done and may differ from sibling monthly fiscal aggregates. | When you need event-level attributes that are not part of the aggregation keys (e.g., event_type, user_id) — those columns are not present, so filtering or grouping by them after reuse is impossible and will silently return wrong counts. | When the cohort should be defined by a different entity than account_id (e.g., customer_id or product_id) — reusing this view will group by the wrong cohort dimension and produce misleading aggregates. | When you need exact timestamp behavior or timezone handling — occurred_date comes from substr(occurred_at,1,10) and date(...); any timezone normalization or ISO parsing issues in occurred_at will be baked into this view and cannot be undone.
params.comparison: use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal instead when you need pre-aggregated monthly or fiscal-period measures — it has aggregation semantics at the monthly/fiscal grain whereas web_events_daily_counts is daily and calendar-date based. | use orders_timeseries_measures instead when you are analyzing order-level time series for sales/orders rather than raw web events — orders_timeseries_measures is designed for order/transaction measures while this view counts web event rows. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched when you need enriched joins between sales facts and dimensions (product, account reps) — that view is JOIN-based and includes enrichment; web_events_daily_counts contains only raw counts and cannot provide joined attributes. | use web_orders_ranked when you need ordering/ranking logic on web-related records (top N, dense_rank over partitions) — web_events_daily_counts is an aggregate and does not preserve the row-level ordering or rank context needed for ranking analyses.

views.description: Daily counts of web events by account and channel. Useful for activity trends and joining to accounts or sales performance. | Use for: Daily activity per account/channel; Correlate events to orders by date/account

views.name: student_transcript_view
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.StdNo,
  s.StdFirstName,
  s.StdLastName,
  e.OfferNo,
  o.CourseNo,
  c.CrsDesc,
  o.OffTerm,
  o.OffYear,
  o.FacNo,
  e.EnrGrade
FROM university_enrollment e
LEFT JOIN university_student s
  ON e.StdNo = s.StdNo
LEFT JOIN university_offering o
  ON e.OfferNo = o.OfferNo
LEFT JOIN university_course c
  ON o.CourseNo = c.CourseNo

params.when_to_use: List all enrollment records for each student-offering pair (transcript-style rows) — i.e., questions that need one row per OfferNo + StdNo with the student name, offering and course details, and the enrollment grade. | Produce transcripts, enrollment rosters, or per-student per-course listings where you expect nulls for missing student or offering metadata (because LEFT JOINs preserve enrollments even if student/offering/course rows are missing). | Join this view to other detail-level tables on OfferNo or StdNo when you intend to keep the enrollment-level grain (not to aggregate within the view). | Filter by OfferNo, StdNo, CourseNo, OffTerm, OffYear, FacNo, or EnrGrade and return matching enrollment rows without pre-aggregation.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use to answer questions aggregated by student (e.g., GPA, course counts per student) without first aggregating at the correct level — WHY: the view is at the enrollment (OfferNo, StdNo) grain; aggregating without de-duplicating or grouping will produce mis-counts if downstream joins duplicate rows. | Do not use to produce offering-level summaries (e.g., headcount per OfferNo, average grade per OfferNo) expecting a single row per OfferNo — WHY: the view contains one row per student enrollment; using it as if it were one row per OfferNo will overcount and produce incorrect aggregates. | Do not use to define a student dimension (one row per StdNo) or to look up canonical student attributes — WHY: StdFirstName/StdLastName come from a LEFT JOIN and may be NULL; also there can be many rows per student (one per enrollment) so treating this as a dimension will duplicate students. | Do not use when you need strictly inner-joined data (only enrollments where student, offering, and course all exist) — WHY: the view uses LEFT JOINs and preserves enrollment rows even if the related dim rows are missing; this can silently include incomplete records. | Do not reuse this view for time-series or fiscal-period aggregated reporting (e.g., monthly/quarterly counts) without first ensuring OffTerm/OffYear are normalized — WHY: OffTerm and OffYear are attributes on the offering; the view does not perform time bucketing or aggregation and may double-count if offerings are joined again downstream. | Do not use as a canonical source of course description or faculty assignment for an offering if you expect those attributes to be authoritative across multiple enrollments — WHY: course and faculty fields are repeated per enrollment; inconsistencies in source data will surface as multiple duplicate rows rather than a single authoritative record.
params.comparison: use course_offering_enrollments instead when you need a view focused on enrollment counts or offering-level enrollment summaries — it likely provides the same enrollment relationship but is designed for aggregated counts (this view is detailed, not aggregated). | use dim_customer_base or dim_product_base analogy: do not use this view as a dimension. Instead, use a dedicated student dimension (if available) when you need one-row-per-student lookups — student_transcript_view is a fact-like enrollment JOIN with many rows per student. | use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal (AGG) style sibling when you require pre-aggregated metrics — this view is raw detail (JOIN) and will produce incorrect results if treated as an aggregated sibling. | use dim_accounts_with_reps or faculty_salary_roster when you need normalized, one-row-per-entity dimension data (student canonical attributes) — those siblings are NORM/JOIN views intended for single-row dimensions, whereas student_transcript_view repeats student attributes per enrollment.

views.description: Student enrollments joined to offerings and courses and optional faculty. One row per enrollment with course, offering, and instructor (FacNo) information and grade. | Use for: Compute GPA or grade distributions for a student; List courses taken by student with offering term/year; Aggregate student performance by instructor or course

views.name: web_orders_ranked
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  account_id,
  occurred_at,
  standard_qty,
  gloss_qty,
  poster_qty,
  total,
  standard_amt_usd,
  gloss_amt_usd,
  poster_amt_usd,
  total_amt_usd,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY datetime(occurred_at) DESC) AS rn_by_account
FROM web_orders

params.when_to_use: Find the most recent web order rows per account (e.g., select the latest order for each account) — this view returns one row per original order with an rn_by_account you can filter to = 1 to get the latest order by occurred_at per account. | Inspect order-level details while preserving original order-level granularity (id is the grain) and see their per-account rank by recency without changing counts or aggregations. | Join order-level attributes (amounts, quantities, timestamps) to other order-grain datasets while also needing the per-account recency position (rn_by_account) computed deterministically from occurred_at.
params.when_not_to_use: As a pre-aggregated customer/month (or any rolled-up) sales summary — this view is at the order (id) grain; summing rows from it without grouping by account and time will double-count if you intend aggregated totals. | To get counts or aggregates per account/cohort directly — rn_by_account is a window column and does not collapse rows; using it without a subsequent aggregation or filter (e.g., WHERE rn_by_account = 1) will not produce per-account aggregates and can silently produce inflated totals. | To represent the latest state of an account when 'latest' is defined by something other than occurred_at — the ranking is strictly ORDER BY datetime(occurred_at) DESC; if 'latest' should use a different timestamp or business rule, re-ranking will be required. | To filter a cohort at the account-level by keeping a single row per account but failing to apply the rn_by_account filter — selecting rows from this view without filtering to rn_by_account = 1 will leave multiple orders per account and thus produce incorrect cohorts or per-account metrics. | As a source for time-series aggregations keyed by a bucketed time period (day/month/fiscal) without explicit bucketing — occurred_at is present but the view does not aggregate by time; using it as if it were pre-bucketed can silently give wrong series. | To compute unique-account counts by using COUNT(id) from this view — COUNT(id) counts orders, not accounts; use COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) or pre-filter to rn_by_account = 1 depending on intent.
params.comparison: use fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal when you need pre-aggregated monthly/fiscal sales totals — that view already provides aggregated amounts at the monthly/fiscal grain whereas web_orders_ranked remains at the order (id) grain and includes a row_number only. | use orders_timeseries_measures when you want time-series aggregates (daily/monthly measures) — orders_timeseries_measures produces aggregated time buckets; web_orders_ranked only contains raw order rows with timestamps and a per-account rank. | use dim_accounts_with_reps when you need account-level attributes or to join representative info at the account grain — dim_accounts_with_reps is account-grain and avoids per-order duplication; web_orders_ranked is order-grain and will duplicate account attributes across orders unless reduced. | use fact_sales_monthly_enriched when you need enriched, joined monthly sales facts — that sibling is already joined and aggregated appropriately for monthly analysis, while web_orders_ranked is best for per-order recency inspection and requires further aggregation to be suitable for monthly reports.

views.description: Orders with row_number per account by occurred_at descending. Exposes row_number to support selecting most recent N orders per account downstream. | Use for: Select recent orders per account (WHERE rn_by_account <= K); Analyze order recency and frequency per account
